// xcel-dashboard: Port 5200, matching vite.config.ts, which pins it with strictPort: true.
One fixed port per dashboard — 5180 Common LMS / 5190 PartnerHub / 5200
XCEL — because all three look alike, so a collision reads as 'the new
dashboard is showing the old project's rows' rather than as an error.
Do NOT add autoPort: a moving port is the thing that convention stops.
configurations.name: xcel-dashboard

// xcel-dashboard-netlify: The SAME app, served through `netlify dev` so the Netlify functions and
Blobs stores are reachable — `npm run dev` is plain vite, which serves no
/api/* endpoint at all. Needed to exercise QA Notes and Links, both of
which author into a Blobs store; under the plain dev server they
correctly report the endpoint as unreachable and hide their composers.
Port 8899 rather than netlify's default 8888, so it cannot collide with
a sibling dashboard doing the same thing.
PORT is pinned INSIDE the command on purpose. vite.config.ts reads
process.env.PORT, and the launcher sets it to this entry's own port — so
without it vite binds to 8899 too and every request reaches vite instead
of netlify's proxy. The symptom is /api/* answering 200 with index.html,
which reads as a routing bug in the app rather than as a port collision.
5201, NOT the 5200 vite.config pins. This entry runs a SECOND vite beside
whatever `npm run dev` already has on 5200 — including one from another
git worktree of this same repo, which is the common case when an agent
run is open. strictPort means the loser dies with EADDRINUSE, and the
error is above the prompt where it is easy to miss.
--functions is an ABSOLUTE path, and it is the load-bearing flag when
this runs inside a git worktree. The CLI resolves the functions dir
against the REPOSITORY root, so from a worktree it serves the main
checkout`s netlify/functions/ and a function added here is simply
missing — /api/<new> then 404s (or falls through to the SPA and answers
200 with index.html), which reads as a broken redirect rather than as
the wrong directory. Both endpoints that already exist in main load
fine, which is what makes it convincing.
configurations.name: xcel-dashboard-netlify
